why: Three complete app screens replace the usual three icons: count more than 60 real values (8 dated import rows, 6 kit toggles, 6 logged or planned sets with load and reps, 22 of 40 min), and note that each screen has a working state change: the flagged row can be fixed, the summary recomputes from the slider, and Log set ticks the row and resets the rest clock.

The chart makes one claim and backs it: 34 monthly points on a 40 to 80% axis with five gridlines, six date ticks and three dated event labels that explain each move, a 64px figure that follows the hover crosshair, and a caption that defines what counts as a session and who is excluded.

All nine cells share one ruled outline and the same title and text rhythm, but each ends in a different proof drawn from plain elements (gap chip, 24-hour muted bar at exact percentages, side view of the plates, 11 load bars with the 2 dips in ink, sync status), so variety comes from the content; the hatched ninth cell breaks the pattern on purpose.

The hero graphic is generated from data, not drawn: 18 named rotation patterns over 84 days are coloured by shift type and past or future, sessions are placed by the app's own rule, and every few seconds one session moves and the caption names the exact change, so notice that the type sits inside the field and the legend explains how to read it.

Eleven named connections are shown as a flow rather than a logo wall: five inputs and six outputs on hand-routed bezier wires with staggered travelling dots in two colours for direction, custom three-tone tiles rather than brand marks, and a three-column definition list below that answers the privacy questions, all in HTML and SVG with no JavaScript.
